HON'BLE KUNAL RAVI SINGH, J.

1. Heard learned counsel for the petitioners; Shri N.K. Pandey, learned Standing Counsel for State respondents and Shri Manu Ghildyal, learned counsel for Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.,
Agra (in short "Nigam").2.

The instant writ petition has been preferred for a direction to respondents to remove 33 KVA Power House from Gata No.168 and vacate the land of the petitioners or to pay the compensation of the said land at the present market rate.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the petitioners are recorded tenure holders of Gata Nos.150, 151 and 168.
The petitioners had offerred Gata Nos.150 and 151 through Gift Deed in favour of Nigam for construction of 33 KVA Power House.

Instead of constructing the power house over Gata Nos.150 and 151, admittedly the respondents have established 33 KVA Power House over Gata No.168 without acquiring or making payment of any compensation for the said land.
Since then the petitioners are running from pillar to post for adequate compensation but till date no reprieve is accorded to them.

4. On the matter being taken up on 10.09.2024, the Court has proceeded to pass the following order:-
"1. Counsel for the petitioners seeks time to indicate whether the petitioners are interested in taking compensation in respect of plot No. 168 over which Sub-Station has been constructed apart from surrendering possession of plot Nos. 150 and 151 of which gift was executed in favour of the State or interested in retaining plot Nos. 150 and 151 and damages for plot No. 168 utilized by the respondents for constructing Sub- Station in place of the plots gifted to them.
2. List this case on 01.10.2024."
5.
Learned counsel for the petitioners states that at present the petitioners are inclined for adequate compensation for Plot No.168 over which 33 KVA Power House has been constructed.

6. Learned Standing Counsel informed to the Court that for redressal of grievance of tenure holders, claiming certain right/title over their land, the State Government had issued detailed Government Order dated 12.05.2016, which provides that in case the claimant files claim supported with requisite documents, the same would be considered by the District Level Committee for ensuring adequate compensation in the light of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (in short the 'Act 2013').

7. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the relief prayed in the instant matter, we dispose of the instant petition with liberty to the petitioners to make fresh representation along with certified copy of the instant order before District Level Committee constituted under the Government Order dated 12.05.2016 within two weeks.
In the event, such representation is made

,
the District Level Committee shall consider the claim of the petitioners and ensure that the proceeding shall be finalised expeditiously, preferably within twelve weeks, thereafter but certainly after taking necessary comments from the Nigam.
